tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you generate a move, check these conditions to avoid illegal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, or moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 5 (smaller), which violates the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Leverage the smallest disk (disk 1) as a temporary holder because it can be placed on any peg without breaking the size rule; move it to free larger disks or to hold a spot needed for later moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg to move larger disks, place the smallest disk on an auxiliary peg that won't be needed immediately.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto a peg that later needs to receive disk 2, causing a blockage.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, leave them untouched and build the remaining tower on top of them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial configuration has a partial correct tower on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 off the goal peg when it is already correctly placed at the bottom.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place disks onto the goal peg one by one in descending size order (largest remaining to smallest), moving each disk only after clearing any smaller disks that block it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you can identify the next largest disk that needs to be placed on the goal peg and can clear its path.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 4 onto the goal peg while disk 3 is still on top of it, violating the descending order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last syntactically correct list of moves in the response is the complete move sequence; any text after it will be ignored by the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the final answer, place the move list at the very end and avoid extra brackets or commentary after it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing an empty answer or placing the move list before additional explanatory text, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, so the move list does not exceed the model’s output token budget.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the puzzle involves many disks or a scattered initial configuration, aim for the minimal number of moves rather than an exhaustive search.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing a very long move list that gets cut off by the token limit, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally simulate each move from the initial configuration and confirm that the final state exactly matches the goal configuration before publishing the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move list, run through the sequence step‑by‑step to catch any mistake.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves disk 2 on a different peg than required, causing the final configuration to differ from the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous sub‑tower of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move three disks directly without first moving the top two to the auxiliary peg, leading to an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking future moves with temporary placements
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When using a disk as a temporary buffer, place it on a peg that will not need to be cleared for later moves, so it does not block the path of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning of intermediate moves, especially when the smallest disk is used repeatedly.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on the auxiliary peg when a later step requires that peg to be empty for moving a larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg is empty or its current top disk is larger than the moving disk; if smaller disks are present, move them away first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to place a larger disk onto a peg that currently has smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which would place a larger disk on a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generating after the reasoning or forget to output the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a move list as the final part of the answer, even if it is empty (but it should not be empty for a solvable puzzle).

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the right disk but forget the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk has a larger number than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of the stack order during mental simulation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit representation of each peg's stack and only select the top disk for moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model generates a long list that exceeds the output length, causing truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Prefer the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves and monitor token usage.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may mis‑track disk locations across moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Update the peg state after each move and verify the disk's presence before moving.
